mode: Edit selected Codex mock-up: tactile Hub-style control refinement
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup / precise-object-edit.
Edit image 1, the selected Tower Codex mock-up, to fix the user's critique: the buttons are flat and disconnected from the actual Copilot Hub world. Produce one finished, full-screen landscape 16:9 game-screen mock-up, without annotations or presentation border. The main visible change MUST be substantial tactile depth and authentic low-poly Hub materials on the interactive controls.

INPUT ROLES: image 1 is the edit target and composition authority. Image 2 is the actual running Hub and controls style reference. Image 3 is the canonical Lab architecture material reference. Image 4 is the canonical noticeboard construction reference. Image 5 is the canonical Developer model; preserve that identity and silhouette.

PRIMARY EDIT — PHYSICAL ANIMATION CONTROLS:
Completely replace the seven flat gray outlined rectangles along the bottom with a row of seven clearly THREE-DIMENSIONAL low-poly push keys mounted into one recessed blue-gray console rail. Make the keys a focal design improvement, readily visible at normal screen size. Each key has a warm ivory top face, a crisp small chamfer, a visible slate-blue sidewall and a short directional contact shadow. These are simple solid geometric parts, as if made by the same artist as the Lab's roof slab, window frames and noticeboard, not photoreal mechanical keyboard caps. A dark socket/gap surrounds each key to make its height physically legible. The button top stays broad and nearly parallel to the screen, with sharp readable dark lettering; the console retains mild perspective and belongs to the bench.
Use these exact labels in order: "Rest", "Idle", "Work", "Move", "Place", "Hit", "Resolve".
Idle only is selected: its top is pale desaturated mint, sitting visibly LOWER inside its socket, with one tiny mint status lamp at its upper edge. No saturated neon green rectangle. The other ivory keys remain raised. A subtle simple pictogram embossed above each label may add character (resting diamond, gentle wave, cog, directional arrows, arrival square, small impact star, dissolving squares); never use a play triangle, pause bars, transport icons, numbers or speed marks. Keep icon detail minimal and crisp. No knobs, cables, rivets, metal screws or ornamental armor.
Retain the small label "ANIMATION", placed above the left of the recessed rail rather than stealing key width. Increase the control-strip height modestly if needed to show depth, preserving a generous uncluttered model area.

SHARED CONTROL FAMILY:
Replace the top-right flat Back to Hub button with a compact raised ivory plaque seated in a slate-blue rim, arrow and dark readable "Back to Hub" label, slight lower/right edge and soft contact shadow. It should echo the actual Hub ambience button's layered lower lip, adapted into the Lab's ivory/blue-gray palette.
Replace the ghost-outline Reset control with a small matching physical ivory key in a blue-gray socket, camera-reset icon and "Reset". Keep it visually secondary.
Make portrait selection feel like real thin dossier plaques on the existing noticeboard, with a small visible thickness and contact shadow; selected Developer uses a restrained mint edge/tab, no neon aura. Do not turn the roster into a webapp card grid.
Unify the stat panel's border and recessed tracks with the same simple matte blue-gray construction. Keep the stats as labeled segmented VISUAL METERS ONLY. Subtle geometric depth in the meter segments is welcome, with no excessive gloss.

PRESERVE ALL APPROVED FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Animation selection only. No speed controls, timeline, scrubber, transport buttons, playback controls, loop checkbox or replay button. Model camera reset is allowed and remains clearly separate.
All stats stay non-numeric: "STATS", "Damage", "Work", "Action speed", "Range", "Compute". No digits, numeric values, units, percentages, upgrade prices, ticks with labels, totals or hidden development badges anywhere. Preserve v03's gauge fill relationships: damage below half, work full, action speed full, range around two-thirds, compute mostly filled.
Keep "Developer", "Direct-output specialist"; character names "Base", "Developer", "Tester", "Analyst", "Security", "Architect", "Linter". Preserve the seven dossier positions. Keep "COPILOT", "TOWER DEFENSE", "COPILOT HUB / TOWER CODEX". Preserve orbit arrows and "Drag to rotate · Tilt · Zoom".
Keep the canonical orange Developer HEAD ONLY, angular swept orange spikes, dark chunky goggles, blue-teal lenses, exactly two cyan face eyes, cream ear disc with curly-brace mark. No body or character redesign.

ART AND WORLD CONTINUITY:
Retain the selected composition: noticeboard on left, floating model centrally on the small plinth, stats on right, physical Lab bench, windows looking into the same campus paths, faceted teal trees and benches. Do not put a duplicate Lab outside the Lab.
Match the actual game's simple matte low-poly faceted rendering, limited ivory/slate-blue/navy/muted mint palette, neutral soft daylight and low-complexity geometry. The buttons must be rendered with the same lighting direction and contact shadows as the modeled bench. Use clear planar bevels rather than glossy gradients. Keep the whole image sharp without cinematic depth of field. No film grain, realistic materials, chromed metal, dramatic bloom or moody spotlights. Preserve the calm playful, approachable campus character. This should feel like the actual game's interactable Lab station, with controls made from its prop kit, not flat HTML rectangles pasted over a pretty illustration.
